verdict.rationale_short: US equity markets (NYSE, Nasdaq) are closed Friday July 3 in observance of Independence Day (July 4 falls on Saturday). No new positions can be initiated or managed today. Overnight, Asia staged a broad recovery: KOSPI +4.65% (complete reversal of Thursday's -4.45% circuit breaker, driven by Samsung and SK Hynix triggering an upside sidecar halt), Nikkei +1.36%, Hang Seng +1.57%, ASX +1.39% — the first coordinated green session since the Korea semiconductor shock. VIX closed the July 2 session at 16.15 (-2.65%), healthier than the night brief's 16.81 estimate, confirming the regime gate is intact going into the holiday. BTC trades ~$61,678 (+2.06%) — approaching but still below the $62,000 re-entry gate; DXY drifts to ~100.78 (-0.08%), remaining marginally above 100. The two defining events of next week: (1) Monday July 6 — first US trading day post-holiday; dual-gate sequence restart attempt (SPX must close >7,460 AND VIX <17); (2) Tuesday July 7 — SPCX Nasdaq-100 inclusion with ~$7.3B in forced passive inflows, the largest single index forced-flow event since Tesla's S&P 500 inclusion in December 2020. June CPI on July 14 is the summer's regime-defining macro event. HOLD maintained until SPX reclaims 7,460 AND VIX holds below 17 on a confirmed closing basis.

Funds must execute by July 6 close, creating pre-inclusion buying pressure on Monday. SPCX at ~$156 (from ~$163 pre-market July 2) gives a materially improved entry. Korea KOSPI +4.65% and VIX at 16.15 reduce the macro headwind for the inclusion-day event. Tesla S&P 500 December 2020 inclusion template shows 8–15% move potential on the forcing day.
trade_setups.entry: Position at ~$156 est. or any holiday-gap dip below $150. Do not chase the July 7 opening spike — sell into forced-flow completion; re-enter on any post-inclusion pullback to $150–155.
trade_setups.invalidation: SPCX reverses below $145 on above-average volume (forced flow already priced or lockup expiry selling dominates) OR SPX gaps below 7,300 on July 6 open (macro overwhelms mechanical bid).

bear_case: The holiday-gap pause provides no fundamental relief from the structural problems July 2 identified. NFP printing 57K with -74K combined revisions to April and May signals employment deteriorating faster than the soft-landing consensus acknowledges. At Nasdaq P/E ~28x, simultaneous slowing growth and sticky June CPI (July 14 — Cleveland Fed nowcasts elevated; Ameriprise forecasts higher) creates a stagflation scenario: the worst multiple environment for long-duration growth equities, where neither rate-cut optimism nor growth narrative provides durable support. TSLA's -7.49% on a 480K delivery beat (18% above 406K consensus, best-ever Q2) is the regime's clearest signal: premium multiples cannot absorb growth-scare narratives regardless of fundamental execution quality. Korea's +4.65% one-day bounce after a -4.45% circuit breaker session is historically consistent with counter-trend rallies that do not end distribution cycles — the distributable float from 80%+ H1 AI semi gains remains large. Counter-argument: VIX closing at 16.15 rather than the night brief's estimated 16.81 is a materially better outcome; if July 6 opens with SPCX bid lifting SPX back above 7,460 and VIX holds below 17, the bear case closes and BUY upgrades for July 7 confirmation. If SPX reclaims 7,460 by July 6 close, the call is wrong.
